newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish air cargo market worth $55 bln - expert. [CORRECTED 10:53 GMT 7/11]
newsitem.headline: Swedish air cargo market worth $55 bln - expert. [CORRECTED 10:53 GMT 7/11]

text.p: Swedish industry which may rely on air freight transportation totals about $55 billion (corrects from $55 million) annually, or about as much as that in Norway, Finland and Denmark combined, an industry analyst said.

Lars Baeckstrom, an aviation industry consultant, told an air cargo industry seminar that Swedish industry excluding agriculture, fishing and forestry, was about the size of its Nordic neighbours combined.
"Sweden's industry is about the size of the other three countries combined.
"The other difference is that there are fewer small and medium size enterprises in Sweden...this also creates different traffic patterns."

Annual freight volumes from Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland total around 450,00 to 500,000 tonnes (corrects figures from "400 to 500 tonnes"), with Sweden accounting for the largest contribution to this total, Baeckstrom said.
Stockholm's Arlanda airport handled the most cargo in the region, followed by Copenhagen's Kastrup, Oslo's Fornebu and Gothenburg's Landvetter, he said.
Stockholm and Copenhagen were the most important regions for the export of high-valued goods. For imports, the pattern was slightly different, with Oslo a very large importer of high-valued products.

Baeckstrom said the Nordic air cargo industry would see a sharp expansion, with the industry average ranging between six and eight percent annual growth. South East Asia would be the most important market.

He said Swedish industry would continue to dominate, there would be increased integration between buyers and sellers on the air freight market, and airlines would separate passenger and cargo sides more.
